security_audit.summary: Most flags describe intended proxy operations, Markdown, or protected credential handling; no evidence found of credential harvesting or prompt injection. The opt-in legacy transport branch exposes reusable tokens without encryption. Rotation also invalidates the old token before local storage checks, risking loss of paid access.

remediation.issue: Opt-in SOCKS5 and plaintext CONNECT expose reusable proxy tokens to network observers.
remediation.suggestion: Remove public plaintext authentication modes or require an encrypted tunnel to the exit. Keep certificate-verified TLS CONNECT as the supported default.

remediation.issue: Token rotation commits remotely before the replacement destination is validated.
remediation.suggestion: Validate the token directory and reserve a private writable staging file before rotating. Preserve replacement credentials privately if final persistence fails.

content.user_title: Manage Paid Proxy Access with x402socks
content.value_statement: Agents may need regional proxy egress without a subscription account. This skill guides approved USDC purchases, token management, and verified TLS CONNECT routing through x402socks.
actual_capabilities: Check service health and list healthy, enabled proxy exits from the live node feed.
Read package prices and decode live payment challenges, rejecting quote amounts above a configured USDC cap.
Guide x402 purchases with explicit approval and TypeScript checks for scheme, network, asset, recipient, domain, and amount.
Store proxy tokens using private files, permission checks, and atomic replacement without placing secrets in process arguments.
Validate tokens, inspect account usage, rotate credentials, and submit signed ownership proofs for recovery.
Test egress IP through TLS CONNECT and provide curl, Python, Node, and browser client examples.
limitations: Purchases require USDC on Base, a signer, and external x402 libraries; the shell helper does not purchase packages itself.
Python payment examples require additional client integration and signing-time validation before unattended use.
Exit availability, prices, session limits, and fair-use quotas depend on the external service and can change.
Proxy routing does not guarantee anonymity or target access; optional legacy transports expose reusable credentials without encryption.

use_cases.title: Verify Regional Application Behavior

use_cases.title: Control Agent Network Spending
use_cases.description: Record approved payment terms, enforce signing limits, and choose a package that matches an authorized automation task.

prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: inspect the service without spending.

prompt_templates.prompt: Quote time_6h with a maximum of 1 USDC. Show payment terms and entitlements, then wait for my approval before signing.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: prepare an approval with an explicit spending cap.

prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: verify an existing paid token.

prompt_templates.prompt: Review my TypeScript x402 integration against approved payment terms. Require signing-time checks and reject unexpected recipients, assets, domains, networks, or amounts.

output_examples.input: A purchase settled but provisioning failed. What should happen next?
output: Do not submit another purchase for the same access.
Retain the settlement transaction hash and prepare a fresh recovery message.
Use the paying wallet to sign the ownership proof, then submit recovery without exposing the signature in command arguments.

best_practices: Approve the full payment terms and enforce them against the actual signing challenge, not only an earlier catalog quote.
Use certificate-verified TLS CONNECT and private token files; keep secrets out of arguments, logs, and chat transcripts.
Check live node health and token validity before retrying; recover settled purchases instead of paying twice.
anti_patterns: Letting a payment wrapper sign arbitrary challenges or treating a package name as unlimited spending approval.
Enabling plaintext proxy authentication on untrusted networks or disabling certificate verification.
Assuming cached prices, exit lists, or single-session packages support unlimited parallel automation.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Running the helper also requires shell access, curl, and Python 3.

faq.question: Can I inspect the service without a funded wallet?
faq.answer: Yes. Health checks, node discovery, catalog lookup, and unsigned challenge quotes do not require purchasing access.

faq.question: Does the helper automatically buy a proxy package?
faq.answer: No. The helper quotes and manages access. Purchases use separately integrated x402 libraries and require explicit approval of payment terms.

faq.question: Which proxy transport should I choose?
faq.answer: Use TLS CONNECT on port 3129 with certificate verification. Legacy SOCKS5 and plaintext CONNECT expose the reusable authentication token.

faq.question: How are proxy tokens stored?
faq.answer: The helper writes tokens atomically to a mode-0600 file in a checked directory. An environment variable is a fallback token source.

faq.question: What happens when payment settles but access is missing?
faq.answer: Do not pay again. Use the settlement transaction hash and a fresh signature from the paying wallet to request credential recovery.
